validity.recommendation: Correct StartState/Province from 'Cairo' to 'Alexandria' (add StartPrefecture/District = 'Al Ameriya'/Amreya). Midor refinery, the pipeline's start point, sits in the Amreya district west of Alexandria -- nowhere near Cairo -- and a ~300+ km Cairo-to-El Hamra distance would be inconsistent with the sourced 140-145 km length.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's current StartState/Province value is 'Cairo', with StartLocation itself blank. This is factually wrong. All independent sources describing this pipeline place its origin at the MIDOR (Middle East Oil Refinery) refinery in Alexandria/Amreya, not Cairo. Daily News Egypt (1 Sept 2025, covering PPC's FY2024/25 general assembly) states explicitly in English: 'a pipeline to transport petroleum products from the MIDOR refinery in Alexandria to the Hamra oil terminal in Alamein.' The Ministry of Petroleum's own FY2023/24 report (petroleum.gov.eg, 24 Sep 2024) and Amwal Al Ghad (4 Aug 2022, covering the Petroleum Minister's site visit) both describe the same 'Midor -> El Hamra' products line without any Cairo reference; Al Arabiya Business (23 May 2024) likewise places Midor refinery 'in the free zone of Amreya, west of Alexandria city' ('بالمنطقة الحرة بالعامرية غرب مدينة الإسكندرية'). No source connects this pipeline to Cairo. EndState/Province ('Matrouh'/El Alamein for the El Hamra terminal) is correct and consistent across all sources -- only the start-side province is wrong.

validity.recommendation: Re-source Owner1 or add Petroleum Pipelines Company (PPC) as the named project owner. Every independent article on this project names PPC ('شركة أنابيب البترول') as the owning company with Petrojet as EPC contractor; none names EGPC directly for this specific line. The current ref (a generic egpc.com.eg 'About EGPC' landing page) does not mention this pipeline at all, so the value/ref pairing is weak even if EGPC-as-ultimate-parent is kept as a matter of tracker convention.
validity.researcher_notes: Current Owner1 = 'Egyptian General Petroleum Corp' (100%), ref = http://www.egpc.com.eg/About_EGPC.aspx -- a generic corporate-history page that does not name the Midor-El Hamra line or any pipeline at all. Every press source found instead attributes the project to PPC: petroleum.gov.eg's FY2023/24 report frames the whole project list (including this line) as achievements of 'شركة أنابيب البترول' (Petroleum Pipelines Company) at its general assembly; Amwal Al Ghad (2022) says the project 'يتبع شركة أنابيب البترول ويجري تنفيذه بواسطة بتروجت' (belongs to PPC, executed by Petrojet); Daily News Egypt (Sept 2025) attributes the project update to 'PPC Chairperson Haggag Rabie' presenting it among 'the company's key projects.' PPC is a wholly state-owned EGPC subsidiary, so recording EGPC as ultimate owner is a defensible convention, not clearly false -- but no source found actually confirms EGPC's specific 100% equity share in this line, only PPC's operational ownership. Flagging for a sourcing fix (either swap to PPC, or keep EGPC but cite a source that actually discusses this pipeline's ownership chain) rather than asserting either is definitively wrong.

validity.recommendation: No change to Length, Diameter, Cost, Fuel, FuelSource, PipelineType, or Status. Keep as 'construction' -- most recent independent coverage (Sept 2025) still describes the project as ongoing, consistent with GEM's construction status carried through Feb 2026.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed. Four independent sources across four different outlets and three years describe the same physical project -- a petroleum-products pipeline from the MIDOR refinery to the El Hamra oil terminal: the Ministry of Petroleum's own FY2023/24 general-assembly report (petroleum.gov.eg, 24 Sep 2024, verbatim: 'إنشاء خط منتجات ميدور / الحمرا بطول 145 كم'), Al Arabiya Business (23 May 2024, an official source quoted on cost/diameter/timeline), Amwal Al Ghad (4 Aug 2022, covering the Petroleum Minister's site visit to Al Hamra port), and Daily News Egypt (1 Sep 2025, PPC's FY2024/25 general assembly, English). None trace back to GEM or to each other as a single wire story -- separate outlets, separate events, separate years. youm7.com (the sheet's existing Fuel/FuelSource ref) reprints the SAME Sept 2024 ministry release as petroleum.gov.eg verbatim, so it is not an independent corroborator, just a mirror. SPEC -- Length: GEM's 145 km matches the ministry's official Sept 2024 figure exactly (highest-tier, most authoritative, and most recent official source). Earlier project-stage estimates (Amwal Al Ghad 2022, Al Arabiya 2024) both cite 140 km -- a minor ~3.5% discrepancy consistent with route finalization between initial planning and the as-built figure reported in the FY2023/24 audited results; treat GEM's 145 km as correct. Diameter (16 in) is corroborated by only one independent source (Al Arabiya, 'يبلغ قطره نحو 16 بوصة') -- medium tier; not found elsewhere (note: petroleum.gov.eg's project list separately mentions an unrelated 16-inch Minya-Asyut doubling line in the same paragraph -- confirmed NOT the same project, do not conflate). Cost (1,700,000,000 EGP) matches Al Arabiya's May 2024 figure exactly ('التكلفة الاستثمارية للمشروع ... تبلغ قرابة 1.7 مليار جنيه'); the lower 2022 estimate (1.3bn EGP, Amwal Al Ghad) reflects normal cost escalation over the project's life, not a conflict. Fuel ('Oil products (only)') and FuelSource ('Midor - Middle East Oil Refinery') are directly confirmed -- the line carries refined products (gasoline/diesel/kerosene, 'البنزين والسولار والكيروسين') out of the MIDOR refinery. PipelineType ('transmission') is reasonable for a 145 km point-to-point refinery-to-export-terminal line, not a gathering/feeder line. DUPLICATE CHECK: compared against the full 46-row Egypt-oil roster -- no other row names Midor or the Midor-El Hamra corridor. P3693 ('El Hamra-Sidi Krir-Alexandria Oil Pipeline', 90 km, dia 16, operating) touches El Hamra but runs the opposite/different corridor (El Hamra to Alexandria via Sidi Kerir) and is an already-operating asset, not this new construction project -- geographically adjacent, not a duplicate.

summary: P7328 (Midor-El Hamra Oil Products Pipeline) is real and well-corroborated (4 independent sources), and Length/Diameter/Cost/Fuel/Status all check out -- but StartState/Province ('Cairo') is a confirmed factual error (should be Alexandria/Amreya, where MIDOR refinery actually sits), and Owner1 (EGPC, via a generic non-specific ref) should likely be re-sourced to Petroleum Pipelines Company (PPC), which every press account names as the actual project owner.
